Drawings, posters, watercolours, photos, prints, etchings or lithographs - everything you ever wanted to know about the graphic arts but were afraid to ask, you'll find here!

Everything you've always wanted to know about graphic arts but never dared to ask is here! Derived from the Greek word graphein (to write), graphic arts refer to all technical processes (drawing, printmaking, graphic design...) used in the visual conception or presentation of an artwork. By extension, they include all image reproduction methods, such as photography. In online graphic art auctions, you’ll find posters, drawings in watercolor, gouache or graphite on paper. These sheets, old or contemporary, where the art of line competes with prints — images reproduced from engraved or drawn supports: engravings, lithographs, silkscreens, etc. The aim is to make an impression. Graphic art sales also give prominence to photography, from albumen paper prints by Gustave Le Gray, Brassaï, Doisneau, Robert Capa, to contemporary works by Nan Goldin or the Magnum agency — even to pieces by street artists whose tags, stencils, and graffiti have moved from the streets to auction rooms and online sales. Did you know? A fake £10 note created by Banksy and handed out for free to the Notting Hill crowd in 2004 can now fetch sky-high prices at Hôtel Drouot. Kaws, Invader, Jonone are also in the spotlight. Classic furniture lovers will find in these sales medieval chests, Renaissance cabinets, and 18th-century stamped commodes (by Charles Cressent, Thomas Hache, B.V.R.B, or Jean-Henri Riesener…) or pieces of excellent craftsmanship. When it comes to entertaining, every detail matters, and table cutlery plays an essential role in offering a unique experience to your guests. Beautiful cutlery not only serves a practical purpose but also adds a touch of refinement and prestige to every meal. Acquiring such sets — especially through auctions — provides an opportunity to find rare and sometimes antique pieces, always rich in history and prestige. These auctions allow you to discover cutlery and tableware that not only stand out for their quality but also tell a unique story, worthy of your most refined receptions. In a world where the art of hosting has become a true expression of personal style, fine cutlery is no longer a luxury but a necessity for those who want to make every dinner a memorable occasion.
